# Results: clock-log formats against allantools

The first and only run of the comparison pre-registered in `PREREGISTRATION.md`, committed
alone as 159334f2 before the fixture existed. The fixture was generated by
`scripts/gen_clock_log_ref.py` with allantools 2024.06 and numpy 2.5.4.

| Bar | Result |
|---|---|
| B1 normalised phase | Met. The `tau0`, grid, gap and fill counts are equal for all three logs; the largest phase difference is 0 s for the TimeLab, TICC and RINEX logs (bar 1e-13 s). |
| B2 estimators | Not met as worded. At every averaging factor allantools evaluates, ADEV, TDEV and MTIE agree within a relative 1.04e-14 (TimeLab), 2.52e-14 (TICC) and 9.90e-15 (RINEX), against a 1e-10 bar. The engine also reports MTIE over the whole record (m = n − 1: 4 096 s, 4 096 s and 122 880 s), which allantools 2024.6 does not evaluate, so one point per log has no oracle value. |
| B3 wiring | Met. The telecom-timing MTIE and TDEV curves from `[series.clock_log]` equal those from the same values as `series.samples`, and the clock kind's `measured` block is absent without the table and leaves the simulated run and its `scenario_hash` unchanged with it. |

By the verdict rule the row stays MODELLED (synthetic logs, a reader oracle by the same
author). `tests/clock_log_allantools.rs` pins these outcomes, including the one unevaluated
point per log.

## Addendum, 2026-10-24: the TICC reference reader is exact

The real-data comparison (`tests/fixtures/clock_log_real/`) found that the engine's TICC reader held each
time stamp as an `f64`, and this fixture's independent reader did the same, so the two agreed (B1 above:
0 s) while both carried up to 4.9e-13 s of rounding at these time stamps. The engine now reads a TICC time
stamp as whole femtoseconds from its decimal text; the reader in `scripts/gen_clock_log_ref.py` now reads
them as exact decimals (`fractions.Fraction`), and `reference.json` was regenerated. The three logs are
byte-identical to before; only the TICC entry of `reference.json` moved (phase by at most 4.9e-13 s, and
the curves computed from it). The TimeLab and RINEX entries are unchanged. No bar was changed: B1 (1e-13 s)
and B2 (a relative 1e-10) hold as before, with the reference now the more accurate of the two.
